captions.detailed: A realistic steel road track bike fork assembly consisting of two straight parallel blades attached to a flat oval-section crown. A threaded steerer tube extends upwards through a black headtube sleeve with silver headset cups, terminating in a silver quill stem with an integrated center expander bolt. Dropped pursuit-style handlebars extend forward and curve downward from the stem collar, finished with black hand grips. The steering mechanism is fully articulated, allowing the fork, stem, and handlebars to rotate together relative to the stationary headtube.
captions.instruction: Generate a CadQuery model of a road track bike fork assembly. It should feature a flat oval-section crown with two straight parallel blades, a threaded steerer tube, a black headtube sleeve, and a silver quill stem holding dropped pursuit handlebars with black grips. Ensure there is a continuous revolute articulation joint to simulate realistic steering motion.
captions.factory: The code constructs three main parts: a stationary frame headtube, a rotating steering assembly, and the handlebars. It uses cylinder primitives to model the headtube and headset cups. The fork is built by extruding a flat oval sketch for the crown, then sweeping or extruding parallel cylinders for the blades, and adding small boxes for the dropouts. The quill stem is created by combining a vertical cylinder, a forward-reaching horizontal cylinder, and a perpendicular collar clamp. The pursuit handlebars are modeled using a 3D wire path swept with a circular profile, capped with cylinder grips. Finally, a continuous revolute articulation is defined along the vertical Z-axis connecting the frame headtube to the rotating fork/handlebar assembly.
